    $x = 42;
    $x = "hello";   // Type error: cannot reassign $x from int to string

That is ordinary php — `php -n` 8.5.6 prints `string(5) "hello"` — and elephc refused it.
`docs/internals/the-type-checker.md` described the refusal as intentional: it let the compiler
know exactly what `$x` was at every point, without needing runtime type tags. The trade is now
made per SLOT rather than per program. Only a local actually reassigned across scalar types
